text:
Gabe H.: Quick follow-up from the Atlas dedicated outage postmortem. Short summary: intermittent edge BGP hold-time oscillation + isolation-controller bug that treated transient origin changes as confirmed split-> triggered full tenant isolation. Impact: ~4h reduced capacity for atlas-dedicated pool. Need owners, timelines, and recurrence detection.

Gabe H.: Proposed actions: 
• Peering hardening (per-peer dampening, neighbor ACLs, keepalive tuning) — owner/ETA?
• Isolation controller fix (debounce + origin-AS cross-check + short-lived allowlist) — owner/ETA?
• Canary automation for on-prem peering (synthetic /24 + traffic validation) — owner/ETA?
• Add telemetry and postmortem dashboard tile (isolation-decisions with context) — owner/ETA?
• Recurrence detection: weekly-pattern detector + auto-ticket on spike (runbook to triage) — owner/ETA?

Marta L.: I can take peering hardening. Plan: add per-peer dampening, keepalive for Atlas neighbors only, and an ACL for customer prefixes. ETA: design + staging tests in 8 days, rollout in 14. Will open RDW ticket.

Devon (runtime): Ill own the isolation controller change. Fix plan: 1) 45s debounce for withdraws, 2) require origin-AS and route-origin consistency for 60s before isolation, 3) implement a short-lived allowlist to avoid blackboxing during maintenance, 4) add unit+integration tests. ETA: hotfix PR in 3 business days, canary in 7 days.

Samir O.: Ill build the canary automation and add smoke checks. Suggest: synthetic /24, canary tenant, run 30m traffic test, then validate KV cache + latency. ETA: harness + scripts in 5 days.

clare-csm: Ill coordinate with Atlas for a maintenance window and request BGP logs for the validation run. Can confirm slot by tomorrow EOD.

rdw-bot: Created Jira: RDW-2609 (atlas-peering-hardening), RDW-2610 (isolation-controller-debounce), RDW-2611 (onprem-canary-automation). Links: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/RDW-2609 , https://jira.redwood.example/browse/RDW-2610 , https://jira.redwood.example/browse/RDW-2611

Gabe H.: More context on recurrence: we saw smaller spikes last 6 weeks that aligned with Atlas nightly backup window. We should add a weekly-pattern detector and flag any deviation >2x baseline.

Devon (runtime): Ill add metrics: isolation_decision{reason="route-change"}, origin_as_mismatch, debounce_latency. Will add alerts: if isolation_decision(route-change) > 1 in 24h for same tenant -> auto-open RDW incident.

Marta L.: Preflight snippet for staging BGP check:
```
# show BGP neighbor summary on staging-edge
ssh ops@staging-edge 'vtysh -c "show ip bgp summary"'
```

Samir O.: Local sim to reproduce churn (test router):
```
# simulate transient withdraws
for i in 1 2 3; do ip route add 198.51.100.0/24 via 192.0.2.$i; sleep 10; ip route del 198.51.100.0/24; done
```

clare-csm: Proposal for detection: alert if >3 neighbor resets in 15m OR if isolation_decision(route-change) triggers for a tenant twice in 24h -> auto-ticket + cc CSM.

Gabe H.: Prioritization: RDW-2610 (controller debounce) = prio:critical, RDW-2609 = prio:high, RDW-2611 = prio:medium. Hotfix must land before any mass isolation policy changes.

rdw-bot: Calendar invite "Atlas peering follow-up" created at 2256789800. Invitees: @Marta L., @Devon (runtime), @Samir O., @clare-csm, @Gabe H.

Marta L.: small note: avoid lowering global hold-times; prefer per-neighbor dampening and keepalive tuning.

Devon (runtime): agreed. debounce + origin checks first. canary then policy if stable.

Gabe H.: Confirm owners & ETAs here by EOD. If blockers, call out now.

Marta L.: confirmed owner RDW-2609, ETA design+staging 8 days.

Devon (runtime): confirmed owner RDW-2610, ETA hotfix 3 business days.

Samir O.: confirmed RDW-2611, ETA harness 5 days.

clare-csm: will lock maintenance window by tomorrow EOD and post update to RDW-2611.

Gabe H.: Thanks all. Ill update the postmortem with these owners and add the recurrence detector to monthly oncall checks. If anything changes, update the Jira ticket and ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
